name: Hydroxylapatite zygoma fixation

card.summary: Use of solid hydroxylapatite blocks to hold a surgically repositioned cheekbone (zygoma) in place while it heals, aimed at a more projected midface.
card.note: Major facial surgery performed by maxillofacial or craniofacial surgeons.

quick.overview:
Hydroxylapatite (HA) zygoma fixation refers to placing a block of hydroxylapatite, a calcium phosphate ceramic, against or between cut sections of the cheekbone to hold it in a new position after surgery. The aim is a more forward or wider cheekbone contour.

HA is the mineral that makes up much of natural bone and is widely used in oral and maxillofacial surgery, according to Wikipedia. Surgical reports on zygomatic osteotomy techniques describe HA blocks as space maintainers while bone heals; these are mainly case series.
quick.how: It is part of surgical osteotomy procedures performed under anaesthesia by specialist surgeons; it is not something done outside a clinic. Healing continues for weeks to months.
quick.risks: As with other facial osteotomies, risks include infection, asymmetry, implant problems and nerve effects, and recovery involves swelling. Individual outcomes depend on the surgeon and anatomy; consultation with a qualified surgeon is the route for any decision.

lead: Hydroxylapatite zygoma fixation is the use of HA, a ceramic with the formula Ca5(PO4)3(OH), as a block or spacer that helps maintain a repositioned zygoma (cheekbone) in cheekbone augmentation surgery such as the zygomatic sandwich osteotomy [1]. In hardmaxxing discussion it is mentioned as a way to bring more projection to the midface.

HA is the main mineral of bone, roughly 65 to 70 percent of bone mass, and Wikipedia describes it as biocompatible, bioactive and osteoconductive and widely used in dentistry and oral and maxillofacial surgery [1]. Surgeons' reports of sandwich osteotomy describe HA as a space maintainer between bone segments until the osteotomy sites ossify, so that the bone itself carries the new contour; these reports are surgical case series.

chain: Surgeon cuts and repositions the zygoma
Bone heals in the new position
angle.text: When the cheekbone is surgically moved to a more projected position, a stable spacer keeps it there during healing. The result is a changed cheek contour.

paras: Hydroxylapatite is a hexagonal calcium phosphate mineral with a Ca/P ratio of 1.67 in its stoichiometric form [1]. It is used as bone filler and implant coating, and nano forms are being researched as scaffolds for bone regeneration [1]. Separately, calcium hydroxylapatite injectable dermal filler (Radiesse) received FDA approval in 2006 [1].

Reports in the surgical literature describe interposing porous HA blocks in zygomatic sandwich osteotomy for malar deficiency, and combining HA granules with collagen in cheek augmentation, with series from various centres. Complication rates reported in these series were low, but evidence is limited to uncontrolled series by individual surgical groups.
No studies found beyond surgical case series; no randomised trials comparing HA fixation with other spacers or fixation methods were identified.

timeline.event: FDA approves injectable calcium hydroxylapatite dermal filler (Radiesse), a separate cosmetic use of the material [1].
